_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); subscription software signals with salesforce.com's rule-T thresholds; the listing rule (CRM listed 2004-06-23)

pit_profile.why: 'We are the leading provider, based on market share, of application services that allow organizations to easily share customer information on demand, according to a December 2006 report by International Data Corporation, or IDC.' 'The market for CRM applications is intensely competitive and rapidly changing, barriers to entry are relatively low, several of our competitors are larger and have more resources than we do, and with the introduction of new technologies and market entrants, we expect competition to intensify in the future.' 'enterprise software application vendors including Amdocs Limited, Infor Global Solutions, Epicor, IBM Corporation, Microsoft Corporation, SAP AG, and Oracle Corporation;' (FY2007 10-K); DURABLE: no 10-K calls the business cyclical ('cycle' appears only as the sales cycle and payment cycles); no disruption theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a subscription software company on this date (OFFSHORE, the one theme live, is scoped to IT services, and the 10-K's cloud computing words, where it has them, describe salesforce.com's own model, not a substitute for it), so the watch list is empty and these words stay here (the PEP obesity rule)

'enterprise software application vendors including Amdocs Limited, Infor Global Solutions, Epicor, IBM Corporation, Microsoft Corporation, SAP AG, and Oracle Corporation;' (FY2007 10-K); DURABLE: no 10-K calls the business cyclical ('cycle' appears only as the sales cycle and payment cycles); no disruption theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a subscription software company on this date (OFFSHORE, the one theme live, is scoped to IT services, and the 10-K's cloud computing words, where it has them, describe salesforce.com's own model, not a substitute for it), so the watch list is empty and these words stay here (the PEP obesity rule). durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.24x; +25% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +0.64; conservative 2yr +140%.

BEAR.desc: EPS +0.0%/yr (worst year FY05-FY08 ex-FY07, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +40.9%/yr (Q1 FY09 guide YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 3.7-yr ex-FY07 median

BULL.desc: EPS +40.9%/yr (FY05-FY08 ex-FY07 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +40.9%/yr (best 2-yr run FY05-FY08 ex-FY07, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: CRM (retrospective, 2008-02-29) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.24x (50.3% downside to Bear $29.67 / +213.2% upside to Bull $187.07) | Adj composite 2.02 vs market 1.39: gap +0.64 [UNDERVALUED] | +25% above the EPP floor $47.77 (147x FY09E $0.33) | Conservative 2-yr case: +140.3% total (+70.1%/yr) | At 183.8x FY09E the 15% hurdle price $78.98 sits at or below the BASE case; revenue +50.4% YoY in Q4 FY08, forward revenues +43.5-44.7% (Q1 FY09 revenue guide (Q4 FY08 release)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
